 JUDGMENT

The petitioners have filed this claim petition U/Sec 166 of M.V. Act, 1989, against the respondents for seeking compensation on account of death of one Sri.Jayanth.D S/o Devarajegowda, in the Motor Vehicle Accident.

02. The brief facts of the case of the petitioners is as under:
That on 28.04.2024 at about 06.20 p.m, the said Jayanth.D was going as a rider in Motor Cycle bearing No.KA-13-EC-6735 along with his friend Dharma, when he reached near Dinesh's Coconut Tree Garden (Thota), Ramenahalli Village,
Arakalagud Taluk, (SCCH-3) 3 M.V.C.No.4441/2024 Hassan District, at that time,
one Car bearing No.KA- 13-MA-2633 driven by its driver, in a rash and negligent manner from Konanur towards Arkalagudu and dashed vehicle of said Jayanth.D.
Due to which said Jayanth.D sustained grievous injuries to head and died on the spot.
Thereafter post mortem conducted in Govt., Hospital, Arkalgud and petitioners have spent Rs.20,000/- towards transportation of dead body and more than Rs.90,000/- towards last rites of the deceased.

Prior to the accident the deceased was hale and healthy and was aged about 23 years and was studying in final year B.E. (Civil Engineering) at Rajeev Institution of Technology, Hassan and was selected in College Campus selection and also running a Tuition and was earning Rs.50,000/- p.m. The deceased was left behind his parents and his sister, who were dependents on his income for their livelihood.
Due to death of the deceased, the petitioners No.1 and 2 have lost their son and petitioner No.3 has lost her lovely brother, are suffering from mental agony which cannot be compensated.

The accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of driver of offending Car and in this regard the Arakalagud Police have registered a case against driver of the offending Car in Cr.No.99/2024 (SCCH-3) 4 M.V.C.No.4441/2024 for the offence punishable U/sec.279, 337 and 304A of IPC.
The respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the said offending vehicle,
are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- to the petitioners together with cost and interest.
03. On service of notice, the respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared before the tribunal through their counsels and filed objections.

04. The respondent No.1 in its objections has denied the entire case of the petitioners and further denied age, income, occupation of deceased and manner of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle, expenses incurred by the petitioners, dependency of the petitioners with the deceased.

While admitting about issuance of insurance policy in respect of Car, restricted its liability subject to Devarajegowda vs Liberty General Insurance Co. Ltd on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57876479/
2 terms conditions of the policy.

sentences.text: It is contended that, the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding valid and effective D.L. RC and Permit at the time of alleged accident.
Hence there is a violation of terms and conditions of the insurance policy.

The alleged accident occurred due to the negligence on the part of the deceased, who was riding a uninsured vehicle without wearing headgear and without valid and (SCCH-3) 5 M.V.C.No.4441/2024 effective driving licence to ride the Motor Cycle in public place and the accident did not take place due to rash and negligence on the part of the driver of the insured vehicle bearing No.KA-13-MA-2633, hence, the petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties.

The compensation claimed is highly excessive, exaggerated and pray for dismiss the petition with costs against respondent No.1.
05.

The respondent No.2 in his objections has denied the entire case of the petitioners and further denied age, avocation, income of the deceased, manner of accident, dependency of the petitioners on the deceased and nature of the injuries sustained by the deceased and expenses incurred by the petitioners.
Further admits that he is the RC owner of the Car and the same was insured with respondent No.1 and the policy was in force and the driver had valid driving licence as on the date of accident.
Hence, the respondent no.1 has to indemnify the respondent no.2.
It is contended that, the compensation claimed is excessive and exorbitant.

Hence, pray for dismiss the petition with costs against respondent No.2.
06.

Based on the aforesaid pleadings, the following issues have been framed by my learned predecessor: -
 (SCCH-3) 6 M.V.C.No.4441/2024  ISSUES
01. Whether the petitioners prove that they are the LRs/dependents of deceased Sri.Jayanth.D S/o Devarajegowda?

02. Whether the petitioners prove that deceased Sri.Jayanth.D S/o Devarajegowda was died on 28.04.2024 at about 6.20 p.m, near Dinesh's Coconut Tree Garden (Thota), Ramanahally Village,
Arkalagud-Konanur Road, Hassan District, due to rash and negligent driving of Car bearing registration No.KA-13-MA-2633 by its driver as alleged in the petition?
03. Whether petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, what amount & from whom?
04 . What order or award?
07. In order to prove their case, the petitioner No.1 was got examined himself as PW.1 and got marked 16 documents as Ex.P.1 to 16 and closed their side evidence.

By way of rebuttal, the respondent No.2 got examined himself as RW.1 and got marked 3 documents as Ex.R.1 to 3 and respondent No.1 did not lead evidence, hence respondent No.1 evidence is taken as nil and closed their side evidence.
09.
Heard both sides and perused materials available on record.

My findings on the aforesaid Issues are as under:-
 Issue No.1: In the Affirmative  Issue No.2: In the Affirmative  Issue No.3: Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.4: As per final order  for the following:-
 REASONS 11. Issues No.1:- Petitioner No.1 filed affidavit in lieu of examination in chief and in his affidavit he has reiterated the entire averments of the petition.
Further stated that, he is the father, petitioner No.2 is the mother and petitioner No.3 is the sister of the deceased.

To prove the said facts, he has produced notarized copies of:- Aadhaar cards of deceased and other petitioners, SSLC and B.E. Civil Engineering marks cards of deceased as per Ex.P.9 to 14 which disclose that the petitioners are the father, mother and sister of the deceased.
There is no dispute in his cross- examination regarding relationship of the petitioners with the deceased.
Therefore, this tribunal considered that, the petitioners No.1 to 3 are the legal representatives and dependents on the income fo the deceased.
Accordingly, this Issue is answered in the Affirmative.
(SCCH-3) 8 M.V.C.No.4441/2024  12. Issues No.2:-
The petitioner No.1 got himself examined as PW.1 and he has given evidence in the form of the affidavit and he has reiterated the petition averments therein.

Though, he has been elaborately cross-examined by the respondent counsel, but nothing is brought on record to disbelieve the case of the petitioners that due to rash and negligent driving of the offending Car by its driver, deceased sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident and died on the spot.
The petitioners have produced documents which are marked at Ex.P1 to 15.

On perusal of the police documents, Ex.P.1 is the FIR registered by the Arakalagud Police against driver of the offending Car in Cr.No.99/2024 for the offence punishable U/sec.279, 337 and 304A of IPC.

Ex.P2 is the Complaint lodged by father of the deceased, which shows that, on the date, place and time of accident near Coconut tree Thota of Dinesh, Ramenahalli, due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending car, the accident took place and deceased died due to accidental injuries.

Ex.P3, Ex.P4 & Ex.P5 are the Spot Devarajegowda vs Liberty General Insurance Co. Ltd on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57876479/
4 Sketch, Spot Mahazar and IMV report which disclose the place of accident and involvement of two vehicles in the accident and damages caused to the vehicles.

sentences.text: It is opined that the accident was not due (SCCH-3) 9 M.V.C.No.4441/2024 to any mechanical defect of the vehicles.
Ex.P.6 is Post mortem report of deceased Jayanth.D shows the cause of death is due to hemorrhage and shock as a result of injury to vital organs (head injury).
Ex.P.7 is Inquest report of deceased Jayanth.D which is not disputed.

Ex.P.8 - Charge sheet shows that, after completion of the investigation the Arkalgud Police have filed charge sheet against driver/respondent No.2 of the offending Car for the offences punishable U/Sec 279, 337, 338 and 304(A) of IPC.

The oral and documentary evidence adduced by the petitioners clearly goes to show that the deceased sustained grievous injuries in a road traffic accident due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending car.
Accordingly, Issue No.2 is answered in the affirmative.
13. Issue No.3:- This issue is related to the entitlement of the compensation on account of the death of the deceased Jayanth.D, who died in the Motor Vehicle Accident.
Due to untimely death of the deceased, the petitioners are put to great financial loss, loss of love and affection and mental agony.
Hence they have filed this petition.
14. To prove the age of the deceased, the petitioners have produced notarized copy of SSLC marks card and Driving licence of the deceased as per (SCCH-3) 10 M.V.C.No.4441/2024 Ex.P13 and 16.
These documents disclose that, date of birth of the deceased as 16.09.2002.
The alleged accident occurred on 28.04.2024 and hence it appears that as on the date of accident the age of the deceased is 22 years.
Therefore, this tribunal has considers the age of the deceased as 22 years on the date of accident.

As per the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Verma and Ors. V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and Ors. case the multiplier applicable to the age group of 15 to 25 years is "18".
15.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: So far as avocation and income of deceased is concerned, the petitioners have produced Ex.P15 Appointment letter issued by M/s Nandi Construction.

It discloses that the deceased Mr.Jayanth .D.
was appointed as Assistant Engineer Grade -1 and said appointment would be effective as of 01-05-2024.

Here the petitioners have not adduced the evidence of author of said Appointment /
offer letter.
The petitioners have produced notarized copies of BE certificates of the deceased, which disclose that the deceased D.Jayanth was the B.E. student.

Therefore, by considering the age,
education qualification and materials available on record, this tribunal has (SCCH-3) 11 M.V.C.No.4441/2024 considers the income of the deceased at Rs.20,000/- p.m and it is multiplied by 18.
16.

In the case on hand, undoubtedly the petitioner No.1 is the father, petitioner No.2 is the mother and petitioner No.3 is the sister of the deceased and they are the dependents on the earnings of the deceased.

In view of the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in (2017)
16 SCC 680 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi & Others case, the future prospects or additional income should be added to monthly income of the deceased.

sentences.text:
The deceased was aged below 40 years at the time of accident, 40% income should be added to the monthly income towards future prospects which would be result in the income to be (20,000 + 8,000) =
Rs.28,000/-.

Since, the deceased was a bachelor at the time of accident, hence 50% of the income Devarajegowda vs Liberty General Insurance Co. Ltd on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57876479/
5 has to be deducted towards personal and living expenses of the deceased and then his monthly income would be (28,000 - 14,000) = Rs.14,000/-.

sentences.text: The income of the deceased for the purpose of determining the loss of dependency would thus be Rs.14,000/-.
As the deceased was aged about 22 years, the multiplier of 18 would have to be applied.
Consequently the claimants (SCCH-3) 12 M.V.C.No.4441/2024 would be entitled for a sum of Rs.30,24,000/- (Rs.14,000 x 12 x 18) towards loss of dependency.

17. In view of the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi & Others case in respect to loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses, the aforesaid amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every 3 years.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi & Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Accordingly, in the head of loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses, 10% is enhanced for period of every 3 years.
18. The claimant No.1 is the father, claimant No.2 is the mother and claimant No.3 is the sister of the deceased.
Therefore, petitioners No.1 & 2 would be entitled for Rs.48,400/- each towards loss of filial consortium.

In view of the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in Magma General Insurance Company Ltd., V/s Nanu Ram alias Churu Ram reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130 and the petitioner No.3 is entitled for Rs.40,000/- under the head loss of love and affection of the deceased brother.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Company Ltd., V/s Nanu Ram alias Churu Ram reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further, the petitioners are entitled for Rs.18,150/- each towards loss of estate and funeral expenses and transportation of dead body.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case (SCCH-3) 13 M.V.C.No.4441/2024 and noticing the number of dependents and 50% of the income taken into consideration towards the personal and living expenses of the deceased, this Tribunal has placed reliance on ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s.
Pranay Sethi & others case has calculated compensation as under;
Head of Compensation Amount in Rupees 1 Loss of (After Rs.
 Dependency 30,24,000-00  deducting 50% of the income  towards personal and living  expenses)
2 Loss of filial consortium (For Rs. 96,800-00  petitioners No.1 & 2)
3 Towards loss of love and Rs. 40,000-00  affection to the petitioner No.3 4 Loss of estate Rs. 18.150-00
Funeral expenses and Rs. 18.150-00  transportation of dead body
Accordingly I hold that, the petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.31,97,100/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.

sentences.text: 20. Regarding liability:-
The respondent No.1 is the Insurer and respondent No.2 is the R.C. Owner of the offending vehicle.

The respondent No.2 got examined himself as RW.1 and got produced RC book of the Car, his Driving licence and Insurance policy of the Car as per Ex.R.1 to 3 which shows the offending Car was stands in the name of respondent No.2 and he had valid driving licence and the policy of the car was in force as on the date of accident.
In the cross-examination RW.1 has admits that he had valid driving licence to drive the car and Police have filed Charge sheet against him.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the insurer and respondent No.2 being the owner of the offending Car are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.

However, since policy of offending vehicle was valid and is in force as on the date of accident, the respondent No.1 being the insurer of offending vehicle shall pay above said compensation amount to the petitioners.
Accordingly, this Issue is answered Partly in affirmative.

21. Issue No.4:- In view of reasons assigned to above Issues, I proceed to pass the following:
 (SCCH-3) 15 M.V.C.No.4441/2024  ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners U/Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 are partly allowed with cost.

The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.31,97,100/- (Rupees thirty one lakh, ninety seven thousand and one hundred only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.1 shall deposit above said compensation amount with interest within two months from the date of this Judgment.

The petitioner No.1 being the father, petitioner No.2 being the mother and petitioner No.3 being the sister of the deceased were apportioned the compensation in the ratio of 40-40-20, in the award amount together with interest.

The petitioners No.1 to 3 are entitled to get release 70% each of the award amount with interest through E-payment directly to their account by obtaining the bank account details and remaining 30% each shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in their Devarajegowda vs Liberty General Insurance Co.
